context.body: Communities, suffering, and final charge · 1 Thessalonians 2:13–16
context.label: Communities, suffering, and final charge

observations.body: Reception of the word is joined to suffering and opposition. For this cause we also thank God without ceasing that when you received from us the word of the message of God, you accepted it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, God’s word, which also works in you who believe. forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they may be saved, to fill up their sins always. But wrath has come on them to the uttermost.

payload.posture: Read 1 Thessalonians 2:13–16 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states reception of the word is joined to suffering and opposition. For this cause we also thank God without ceasing that when you received from us the word of the message of God, you accepted it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, God’s word, which also works in you who believe. forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they may be saved, to fill up their sins always. But wrath has come on them to the uttermost. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
